Read History Go to My Account Log Out News NSCDC parades four suspected cable thieves arrested in Abuja The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Command, has paraded four suspected electrical cable vandals
Listen to this article Share The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Command, has paraded four suspected electrical cable vandals arrested in separate operations in Abaji, Kubwa and the Wuye axis of Abuja. The suspects were arrested over alleged vandalism, unlawful possession and trafficking of electrical installation cables and armoured cables, as the corps intensifies efforts to protect critical national assets and infrastructure across the FCT. Olusola Odumosu, FCT Commandant of the NSCDC, disclosed this in a statement issued by the command, saying the arrests followed intelligence-led operations by its anti-vandal patrol team and officers attached to the Critical National Assets and Infrastructure Department. According to the command, the operations led to the recovery of bundles of high-tension aluminium conductor cables suspected to have been removed from Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) installations, electrical installation wires and armoured cables, alongside tools allegedly used in the suspected offences. In the first case, the command said its anti-vandal patrol team, acting on credible intelligence, arrested a 44-year-old man identified as Mammed Nuhu around the residential quarters in Abaji Area Council. Nuhu, who hails from Basari Local Government Area of Katsina State, was arrested over the alleged unlawful possession and storage of high-tension aluminium conductor cables suspected to have been vandalised from electricity infrastructure in the area. The statement said preliminary investigations indicated that Nuhu allegedly disclosed that two other individuals, identified as Saifullah, 33, and Abdulraham, 25, had brought the cables to him for safekeeping pending their sale to prospective buyers. The two alleged accomplices are currently at large, while the command said efforts were ongoing to apprehend them and identify other individuals suspected of involvement in the alleged criminal activity. Bundles of high-tension aluminium conductor cables suspected to have been removed from AEDC installations in Abaji were recovered during the operation. In a related development, NSCDC operatives attached to the Kubwa Base Station arrested two men over the alleged vandalism and unlawful possession of electrical cables around Government Secondary School, Kubwa. The suspects were identified as Amos Makama, 27, from Kokona Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, and Ibrahim Mohammed Maitama Inuwa, 27, from Dala Local Government Area of Kano State. According to the command, the arrests were made at about 1 a.m. following reports of suspicious movements around the school’s perimeter fence by commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators working in the area. The statement said Makama, described as the principal suspect, allegedly gained access to the school through its gate in the evening and proceeded to cut electrical wires in the school buildings. He reportedly remained within the premises until about midnight before attempting to escape by climbing the fence with the cables, with the intention of selling the materials. During interrogation, Makama allegedly disclosed that he had contacted Inuwa, whom the command identified as the prospective buyer. Inuwa was said to have made an advance payment of N35,000 for the cables. The command said its operatives subsequently apprehended Inuwa after establishing contact with him in connection with the proposed transaction. Both suspects reportedly confessed to their involvement in the alleged activity and disclosed that they had been engaged in the business since 2024, according to the statement. The third case involved the alleged conspiracy, vandalism and theft of armoured cables near Berger Roundabout along the Wuye axis of Abuja. Odumosu said officers of the command’s Critical National Assets and Infrastructure Department were alerted by members of a local vigilante group to suspicious activities involving some individuals in the area at about 10.30 p.m. The information led to the arrest of Suleiman Jafaru, who was allegedly removing armoured cables from the roadside near Berger Roundabout. The command said armoured cables and two diggers were recovered from the scene. Preliminary investigations indicated that three individuals were allegedly involved in the suspected vandalism and removal of the cables, with Jafaru claiming that two other persons who accompanied him escaped during the operation. The identities and whereabouts of the two alleged accomplices remain unknown. Odumosu condemned the alleged vandalism of electricity installations, describing it as an attack on the welfare, safety and economic well-being of residents of the FCT. He said the destruction and theft of electrical infrastructure disrupt electricity supply, impose additional costs on service providers and communities, and divert resources that could otherwise be invested in improving electricity services. “The cost of replacing stolen cables and repairing damaged installations also diverts resources that could otherwise be invested in improving electricity services,” Odumosu said. He added that the alleged involvement of individuals who receive and purchase stolen electrical materials highlighted the need to address the market that sustains infrastructure vandalism. The commandant reiterated that the NSCDC would pursue not only those who physically remove electrical cables but also individuals who knowingly purchase, receive or facilitate the sale of stolen materials. He said the FCT Command remained committed to intelligence-led operations and stronger collaboration with relevant stakeholders to protect critical national assets and ensure that suspects found culpable were brought to justice through due process. Odumosu urged residents, community leaders, commercial motorcyclists, tricycle operators, traders and scrap-metal dealers to remain vigilant and report suspicious activities around electricity installations to the appropriate authorities. The command said it would sustain its efforts to curb cable vandalism and protect infrastructure essential to electricity supply, public safety and economic activities across the Federal Capital Territory.
